# FruitFacts AI Instructions

FruitFacts is a website for indexing useful fruit variety information for home
gardeners, with an emphasis on cited source data from university extension and
land grant publications rather than uncited editorial summaries

The main goal is to help gardeners search, compare, and chart varieties by
traits such as harvest/ripening time, patent status, source references, and
locations where varieties have been grown or recommended

## Repository Shape

- `plant_database/` contains the source data in JSON5
  - `plants/` has base variety/type data
  - `references/` has imported publications, trial reports, nursery lists,
    garden lists, and other source collections
  - `types.json5` defines plant type metadata
  - `help_needed.md` is generated by the backend import process. Do not edit it
    by hand
- `backend/` is a Rust Actix Web API backed by SQLite and Diesel
- `frontend/` is a Next.js/React app
- `server_admin/` contains old Ubuntu/nginx/systemd deployment helpers
- `.dvc/` tracks large files such as original PDFs and generated thumbnails

## Data Principles

- Preserve source meaning. Do not convert vague source dates like "mid
  September" into exact dates unless the source did so
- Prefer adding citations and cross references over paraphrasing source
  publications
- Keep the JSON5 data human-editable for semi-technical contributors
- Use existing field names and nearby examples before inventing new schema
  shapes
- If a data file says `needs_help`, leave the marker unless the underlying data
  issue is genuinely resolved
- Do not manually edit generated Rust schema files or generated data summaries
  unless the generation path itself is being repaired

## Backend

- Work from `backend/`
- Local setup normally needs:
  - Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill real secrets only when OAuth is
    needed
  - Ensure `src/gazetteer_load/2021_Gaz_zcta_national.txt` exists. For tests,
    the demo fixture can be copied from
    `src/gazetteer_load/test_data_file.txt.demo`
- Useful commands:
  - `cargo test --lib --no-default-features`
  - `cargo test --lib --no-default-features test_database_loading -- --ignored`
  - `cargo build --no-default-features --bin harvest-chart-server`
  - `cargo run --no-default-features --bin harvest-chart-server -- --reload_db`
- The PDF/thumbnail support tools are optional support binaries. Keep server
  builds and tests able to run without PDFium or image-generation dependencies
- If changing database schema, update Diesel migrations and generated schema in
  the established project style
- Avoid broad rewrites in `import_db.rs`; it is large and central, so keep
  changes scoped and covered by an import/load test when possible

## Frontend

- Work from `frontend/`
- This is a Next.js pages-router app using React, Tailwind, MUI, Leaflet, and
  chart components
- Useful commands, once Node dependencies are installed:
  - `npm install`
  - `npm run dev`
  - `npm run build`
  - `npm test`
  - `npm run lint`
- In Windows Codex sessions, bare `node` or `npm` may be absent from the
  inherited `PATH` even when the repo-local Node install exists. Before
  reporting Node missing, prefix Node/npm commands with
  `.\helper_scripts\dependency_env.ps1 -Name node -Quiet;` from the repo root,
  for example
  `.\helper_scripts\dependency_env.ps1 -Name node -Quiet; node -v; npm -v`.
  The helper checks the FruitFacts local Node install, Codex's Node runtime,
  normal Windows Node install paths, and `PATH`.
- Local development expects the backend base URL from `.env.development`,
  typically `http://local.fruitfacts.xyz:3001`
- Keep pages functional and simple. The intended audience includes ordinary
  gardeners, not only developers
- Avoid adding marketing-style landing pages. The site should expose search,
  browsing, maps, charts, and cited reference data directly

## DVC And Large Files

- DVC stores reference PDFs and frontend thumbnail images
- The configured remote is a Google Drive remote. The credential file
  `michael-gdrive-credentials.json` is intentionally not committed
- To restore assets on a fresh checkout:
  - Install DVC with Google Drive support, for example `pip install dvc[gdrive]`
  - Place the service account JSON where `.dvc/config` expects it
  - Run `dvc pull` from the repository root
- Do not commit restored PDFs or thumbnails directly. Commit the `.dvc` pointer
  files after adding or changing large assets
- After generating new thumbnails, use the existing DVC workflow or a modernized
  replacement script, then commit both data changes and `.dvc` pointer changes

## Scripts And Tooling

- Several existing helper scripts are for server deployment. Do not remove or
  rewrite them casually
- Review helper scripts before running them. Some older scripts intentionally
  update tools, rebuild databases, touch server services, or deploy to nginx
- Keep new scripts small and explicit
- Keep scripts cross-platform where practical, or provide clearly named Windows
  and Unix variants

## Code Quality And Testing

- Do not use emoji anywhere, not in code, not in comments, not in markdown
  files
- Do not use em dashes anywhere, but especially not in scripts
- In printlines/comments, do not end self-contained sentences, especially those
  that already end with a newline, with a period. For example:
  `Write-Host "No lobbies to join"`
- Keep to printable ascii wherever possible
- Avoid UTF-8 with BOM files. Use plain ascii or UTF-8 without BOM
- Always create a plan as step 1 of any block of work. If a persistent plan file
  is useful, put it under `ai_tool_plans/` at the repo root and mark completed
  phases as work proceeds
- Attempt to minimize line count to some extent. Do not take this to an
  extreme, but avoid abstractions that are just wrappers, duplicated code, and
  other verbose things
- Mimic the style of the existing code
  - Backend code is Rust using Actix, Diesel, SQLite, and fairly direct module
    organization
  - Frontend code is JavaScript/React pages-router Next.js with simple
    components
  - Data files are JSON5 and should stay readable for semi-technical
    contributors
- Add simple, high-level integration tests to catch regressions and document
  high level functionality. It is not necessary to add tests for every little
  function unless the function has tricky edge cases or is complex by itself
  - Make every effort to include at least one integration test, smoke test, or
    extension of an existing one with each major set of changes, and include it
    as a final phase of work
  - Do not just write the test. Include a run of the actual as-written test and
    fixes until it passes
  - Add tests or easy rerun helpers for backend import/database behavior,
    frontend flows, DVC/thumbnail tooling, and user-list features as those areas
    are changed
- Watch for duplicated concepts across backend, frontend, and data import code,
  such as path encoding, plant type names, date/ripening parsing, user lists,
  locations, and collection items. If behavior changes, update every relevant
  copy or centralize new code in a way that keeps the change set smaller
- For edits to generated schema/data outputs, take extra care to confirm whether
  the generated file or the generator should be changed
- New code should be as free of compiler and linter warnings as possible
  Warnings are not all treated as errors, but do a second pass to remove
  avoidable warnings after building
- New code should have formatting linters run on it. Prefer a scoped pass over
  the files or smallest directories touched by the change when the tool supports
  it
  - Backend: use `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --no-default-features --bin harvest-chart-server`,
    and focused `cargo test` commands as appropriate
  - Frontend: use `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, and scoped
    Prettier commands such as `npx prettier --write path/to/file` when Node is
    available
  - JSON5/data: prefer a parser-backed check or the backend import/database load
    test over ad hoc string manipulation
- Use full unscoped formatting or dependency update passes only for broad
  formatting changes, formatter/linter config changes, release-style
  validation, or when a scoped pass indicates wider cleanup is needed
- File-mutating formatter/linter commands can take time. Do not treat them as
  done until the process has fully exited
- Before starting another cleanup or validation pass after any timeout or
  interrupted run, check for stale formatter, linter, Cargo, npm, or server
  processes that could interfere with the next run
- If a command cannot be run because local tooling is missing, say so plainly
  and record the missing prerequisite
- If DVC assets are unavailable, note that thumbnail/PDF behavior could not be
  fully verified

## Dependency Guidance

- Dependency versions in manifests are deliberately pinned exactly
- Do not add or require lockfiles unless explicitly asked
- Do not blindly run dependency-upgrade scripts as part of ordinary cleanup
- Upgrade one ecosystem at a time and verify with build/test commands
- Keep optional PDF/thumbnail dependencies separate from the normal backend
  server path

## Common Workflows

- Restore backend smoke test:
  1. Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env`
  2. Copy the demo gazetteer file if the real one is unavailable
  3. Run `cargo test --lib --no-default-features`
  4. Run the ignored database load test
  5. Build and run `harvest-chart-server` with `--no-default-features`
- Restore large files:
  1. Install DVC with Google Drive support
  2. Restore the service account credential file outside git
  3. Run `dvc pull`
  4. Verify that PDFs and `frontend/public/data/**/*.jpg` files exist
- Resume frontend:
  1. Install the recorded or chosen Node version
  2. Install dependencies
  3. Build against a running backend or a clearly configured API URL
